# nemau_quotas (Data Source)

The capacity limits applied to the configured credential.

A write is admitted only when the project and the organization that owns it both have room. Without `scope`, each dimension is reported once, for the scope that will refuse first: the one with the least headroom, which does not always have the smallest limit.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "nemau_quotas" "current" {}

# Room left in each dimension, in that dimension's unit.
output "quota_available" {
  value = { for dimension in data.nemau_quotas.current.dimensions : dimension.name => dimension.available }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `scope` (String) Report a single scope, `project` or `tenant`, instead of whichever one binds per dimension.

### Read-Only

- `dimensions` (Attributes List) One entry per limited resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dimensions))
- `project_id` (String) The project the credential resolved to, empty when it resolves to none.

<a id="nestedatt--dimensions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dimensions`

Read-Only:

- `available` (Number) `limit - used - reserved`, never negative.
- `limit` (Number) The limit, in `unit`.
- `name` (String) What is limited: `instances`, `cores`, `ram`, `volumes`, `volumeSize`, `snapshots`, `networks`, `subnets`, `floatingIps`, `securityGroups`, `loadBalancers` or `objectStorage`.
- `reserved` (Number) Capacity claimed by operations admitted but not yet finished. The platform counts it against the limit.
- `scope` (String) `project` or `tenant` (the organization).
- `unit` (String) `count`, `MB`, `GB` or `bytes`. RAM is counted in MB and volume size in GB, so one unit cannot be assumed for both.
- `used` (Number) Capacity in use, in `unit`.
